Hamilton系へのリンクは調和ポテンシャルの力学部分です。計算には摩擦・雑音またはCSVRの温度浴が追加されます。 Hamilton系・振動子 q˙=∂H∂p,p˙=−∂H∂q H=p22+V(q) 正準方程式と分離可能なHamiltonianの代表形。調和・4次ポテンシャルの振動子で、エネルギー誤差とシンプレクティック性を比べます。 スカラーItô拡散：GBMとOU dXt=a(Xt,t) dt+b(Xt,t) dWt GBM: a=μX, b=σX;OU: a=κ(θ−X), b=σ 決定論的初期値のスカラーSDE。平均・二次モーメントの弱誤差、共有Brown運動での強誤差、有限標本のMCSEを分けます。OUは調和Langevin系の浴成分に関連する追加検査です。 実行例で使う式 補助実行例実行例の定義・検証式 Langevin温度制御：正準分布・刻み偏り・時間相関 dq=p text.en: NUMERICAL METHODS ATLAS · PROBLEM Langevin thermostat: canonical distributions, timestep bias and correlation Explore this problem’s equations, reference conditions, methods and published code. Saved result figure Stored harmonic-BAOAB steps 0.4/0.2/0.1 separate discrete stationary-covariance bias, sampling error, canonical-CDF errors and position correlation at lag 2. Equations and problem definitions The Hamiltonian link identifies the harmonic mechanical part; the calculations add friction/noise or a CSVR heat bath. Hamiltonian systems and oscillators q˙=∂H∂p,p˙=−∂H∂q H=p22+V(q) Canonical equations and a representative separable Hamiltonian. Harmonic and quartic oscillators distinguish energy error from symplecticity. Scalar Ito diffusion: GBM and OU dXt=a(Xt,t) dt+b(Xt,t) dWt GBM: a=μX, b=σX;OU: a=κ(θ−X), b=σ Scalar SDEs with deterministic initial states. Separate weak moment bias,strong errors on shared Brownian paths and finite-sample MCSE. OU is a related bath-component check,not the full harmonic Langevin system. Formulations used by execution examples Supplementary execution exampleExample definition or validation formula Langevin thermostat: canonical distributions, timestep bias and correlation dq=p dt,dp=−ω2q dt−γp dt+2γT dW Σ=MΣMT+Q,Σh=diag⁡(T/ω2,T(1−h2ω2/4)) Compare harmonic BAOAB with canonical and discrete-Lyapunov stationary distributions, and with continuous/discrete time correlations. Supplementary execution exampleExample definition or validation formula CSVR versus Langevin: distributions, fluctuations and correlations of two harmonic modes U(q)=12∑i=12ωi2qi2,H=K+U,γ=12τ Σh,i=diag⁡(Tωi2(1−h2ωi2/4),T),Σh=MΣhMT+Q K∼Gamma⁡(1,T),H∼Gamma⁡(2,T),Var⁡K=T2,Var⁡H=2T2 CX(t)=E[(Xt−μX)(X0−μX)]σX2,SE⁡(C^X)=sproductsNreplicas Compare global CSVR with local Langevin on two nondegenerate modes using the same OBABO splitting. Record position, momentum, temperature and total-energy distributions, fluctuations and correlations. Supplementary execution exampleExample definition or validation formula OU weak moments with joint Brownian coupling dXt=κ(θ−Xt) dt+σ dWt bp(h)=E[Xh(T)p]−E[X(T)p],p=1,2 Cov⁡(Jh,ΔW)=(1−e−κh)/κ Separate continuous truth,exact discrete EM expectation,paired-path weak difference and MCSE. Exact and reference solutions Use analytic canonical-distribution, moment and correlation standards for the harmonic potential to check timestep bias, separately from frictionless, noiseless harmonic trajectories. Analytic referenceRelated-model reference OU weak moments with joint Brownian coupling dX_t=\kappa(\theta-X_t)\,dt+\sigma\,dW_t; b_p(h)=\mathbb E[X_h(T)^p]-\mathbb E[X(T)^p],\quad p=1,2; \operatorname{Cov}(J_h,\Delta W)=(1-e^{-\kappa h})/\kappa dX=1.5(.2-X)dt+.8dW,X0=.7;dimensionlessT1;8/16/32/64steps;32independent seeds×1024paths. Unbounded state,no clipping. dX=1.5(.2-X)dt+.8dW,X0=.7;dimensionlessT1;8/16/32/64steps;32independent seeds×1024paths. Unbounded state,no clipping. References and results of execution examples Supplementary execution example Langevin thermostat: canonical distributions, timestep bias and correlation Check against a SciPy discrete-Lyapunov solve and explicit harmonic covariance diag(T/omega²,T(1-h²omega²/4)). Separate second-order momentum bias from sampling error and evaluate burn transients from the map. A separate matrix exponential gives continuous correlation. Saved result / JSON Reference and validation details → Supplementary execution example CSVR versus Langevin: distributions, fluctuations and correlations of two harmonic modes Check canonical Gaussian/Gamma distributions and K/U/H means/variances. For finite steps, compare the Verlet-shadow position variance T/[omega²(1−h² omega²/4)] and momentum variance T against a separately constructed Lyapunov solution. Deterministic biases at h=0.2/0.1/0.05 establish second order. Check Langevin q,p,K,H correlations against independent discrete propagation; report CSVR correlations with independent-replica standard errors and tau/h dependence. Saved result / JSON Reference and validation details → Supplementary execution example OU weak moments with joint Brownian coupling Before paths qualify Decimal80/120,independent GH/OUcovariance integrals and paired-variance allocation. Gate5MCSE calibration,MCSE precision,fixed three-level weak rate and final-two-level3SE resolution. Coverage is descriptive over32batches against discrete truth. Saved result / JSON Reference and validation details → Numerical methods Methods from explicitly bound supplementary examples and, where present, the common execution example. No release for a different problem is borrowed. Methods used by this problem’s execution examples Langevin thermostat Method-registry status: Educational example / related code Stochastic velocity rescaling (CSVR) Method-registry status: Educational example / related code Stochastic differential equations Method-registry status: Educational example / related code Code and execution Supplementary execution example Langevin thermostat: canonical distributions, timestep bias and correlation Compare harmonic BAOAB with canonical and discrete-Lyapunov stationary distributions, and with continuous/discrete time correlations. Conditions, commands and validation scope Assumptions Mass, Boltzmann constant, frequency, friction and temperature are one. Use 32768 replicas, burn time 20, steps 0.4/0.2/0.1 and correlation lag 2; require h*omega<2. Use these commands in the working directory specified by the execution guide after extracting the ZIP. A command may execute several cases in the package. python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python -m pytest -q python run.py --input inputs.json --output output Validation limits Distribution checks use a harmonic potential and fixed seeds. Exact position variance does not remove finite-step momentum bias. Evidence does not transfer to other thermostats, general molecules or long ab initio MD. Package source and tests These lists include files shared across the package; they are not all dedicated to this problem. Record position, momentum, temperature and total-energy distributions, fluctuations and correlations. Conditions, commands and validation scope Assumptions m=kB=T=1, omega=(1,1.7), Nf=2. tau=0.25/1, h=0.1/0.05. Evolve 8192 canonically initialized replicas and a separate 4096-replica ensemble with q,p scaled by 1.4 to t=20. Correlation lags are 0/0.5/1/2/4. Use these commands in the working directory specified by the execution guide after extracting the ZIP. A command may execute several cases in the package. python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python -m pytest -q python run.py --input inputs.json --output output Validation limits Global-CSVR and local-Langevin dynamical correlations are not required to agree. CDF errors are maxima over five declared points, not whole-line KS distances. Canonical-start preservation and the heated-start finite-time check do not prove ergodicity; tests retain an invariant unexcited-axis counterexample. No extrapolation to molecules, constraints or BOMD. Package source and tests These lists include files shared across the package; they are not all dedicated to this problem.
